title: Workflows Guidebook
text:
Welcome!
Welcome to the Workflows Guidebook! This document outlines key information about the Workflows team and our main project: developing tools that facilitate the stock assessment reporting process. We are located within the National Stock Assessment Program (NSAP) and are guided by a Steering Committee.
Please use the links on the sidebar (left) to navigate this website and learn about the Workflows team and our Steering Committee.

title: The Steering Committee
text:
The current members of the Steering Committee are:

Ben Williams (AFSC)
Daniel Hennen (NEFSC)
Kiva Oken (NWFSC)
Eli Holmes (NWFSC)
Lisa Ailloud (SEFSC)
Caitlin Allen Akselrud (SWFSC)
Megumi Oshima (PIFSC)
Michelle Sculley (PIFSC)
Kelli Johnson (HQ OST)

Each member of the team was initially chosen for their historical involvement with the development of a reproducible workflow for their respective region and their expertise with stock assessments. The committee aims to represent a diverse range of perspectives from NOAA Fisheries Science Centers and offices.


The Steering Committee is joined by the current stock assessment Workflows Team which governs this group.



Steering Committee members have the option to rotate off of the group given they provide a sufficient replacement before their departure. This ensures continuity and the infusion of fresh perspectives within the committee.
An annual review is will be conducted to provide opportunity for the Steering Committee to evaluate their membership and discuss any potential changes. This review will also allow the Workflows Team to assess the effectiveness of the committee and make adjustments as needed.
When a member decides to step down from the Steering Committee, they are encouraged to recommend a suitable replacement from their organization or network. The recommended individual should possess relevant expertise and a commitment to advancing reproducible workflows within NOAA Fisheries.

title: Project Folder Navigation
text:
Project Folder Navigation
The “Steering Committee” project folder can be found in your “Shared Drives” folder in Google Drive. This folder contains important documents and resources related to the Steering Committee’s activities, including meeting notes, agendas, and other relevant materials.
The following folders contain the most relevant resources:

Call agenda/notes
Conference abstracts
Implementation plans
Manuscripts



Meeting Notes
Meeting notes from previous Steering Committee meetings are editable by the Steering Committee and internal NOAA HQ team. These notes provide a record of discussions, decisions, and action items from past meetings.
Each meeting, a new section is added to the document with the date and agenda items discussed. Steering Committee members are encouraged to review the notes from previous meetings to stay informed about ongoing discussions and initiatives.


Additional Documents
Over time, we have utilized Google docs to organize and draft important documents for the Steering Committee. These documents record the key processes and decisions made by the Steering Committee during the project’s development.

title: Contributing
text:
Ideas and feedback welcomed here!
Do you have an idea that would improve this guidebook? Consider making a contribution! We welcome ideas for improving any other material associated with this guidebook.






Tipasar and stockplotr



Please read our Contributing guides for asar and stockplotr if you’d like to contribute to those packages.




Recommended workflow: fork & submit a pull request
The most efficient way to contribute an idea is to fork this repo, make your suggested changes on a local branch, and then submit a pull request to the main branch. This will allow the developers to easily evaluate your suggested changes. Please see the GitHub Docs’ “Contributing to a project” page for step-by-step guidance in using this workflow.


Recommended practices

Write clear, succinct commit messages (see some tips here)
Limit a commit to a few, rather than many, changes. Smaller commits means more commit messages, which is often helpful for documentation.
Ensure your base branch is correct. We merge all branches into main.
Test that your contributed code will function as expected under different circumstances.
Add comments to the code if it’s not immediately clear what the purpose of the code is, or how it works.



Contributing bugs
Found a bug? Tell us about it on our Issues page. If possible, please submit a reproducible example (reprex) to help us understand the problem better and, ideally, allow us to reproduce your issue.


Ask if you need help!
If you’re unsure about how to contribute, just ask us for help. We’d be more than happy to guide you.

title: Role of the Steering Committee
text:
The Steering Committee serves as an advisory group to provide strategic guidance, feedback, and expertise on workflows related to stock assessment at NOAA Fisheries. The committee’s primary role is to ensure that the development and implementation of reproducible workflows align with the needs and priorities of NOAA Fisheries Science Centers and offices.
The Steering Committee members are expected to:

Attend monthly, virtual meetings to discuss project updates, challenges, and opportunities
Review and provide feedback on project plans, documentation, and deliverables
Share insights and best practices from their respective regions and areas of expertise
Advocate for the adoption of reproducible workflows within their organizations
Collaborate with the Workflows Team to identify and address any barriers to implementation

Please see the membership section for information on what a Steering Committee member is responsible for doing when they are no longer able to serve on the committee.

Code of Conduct

Our Pledge
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.
We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.


Our Standards
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
Public or private harassment
Publishing others’ private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

This Code of Conduct is an abbreviated version of the {asar} code of conduct, which was adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1.

title: Role of the Steering Committee
text:
Processes for getting involved
Steering Committee members are encouraged to actively participate in discussions, provide feedback, and contribute to the development of reproducible workflows. Members can get involved by attending meetings, reviewing project materials, and engaging in discussions through email or GitHub. We also encourage Steering Committee members to contribute previous code that is adaptable to the project or through a pull request if they so choose.
The Workflows Team is actively working on adding more opportunities for Steering Committee members to get involved in the project through the use of detailed and actionable GitHub issues on the repositories page. Please see the {stockplotr} issues page or {asar} issues page for potential tasks, and our contributions guide, if you are interested in contributing.

title: Meeting Schedule and Communication
text:
Meeting Schedule and Communication
The Steering Committee meets virtually on the second Tuesday of each month at 3:30 PM Eastern Time. Meeting invitations, agendas, and notes, and any other important materials are sent out in advance to all committee members. Meetings are based on need, so it is not uncommon during the development process when no feedback is needed to cancel the meeting.
During meetings, Steering Committee members are encouraged to use the raise hand feature to contribute to the discussion or utilize other Google meets features like reactions (i.e., thumbs up) or chat to add their input.
Communication with the Steering Committee is made through email, Google chat space and GitHub discussions for {asar} and {stockplotr}.


Meeting Planning
Meeting topics and agenda are planned up to one week in advance by the Workflows Team. The topics are contingent on need and any topics that might have come up throughout the month before the meeting.
Occasionally, a request to discuss a topic from an outside party may arise and, when relevant, it will be added to the agenda.
Steering committee members are encouraged to preview the agenda or add their own topics when the need arises.


Feedback Deadlines
When review or feedback is request on the project for the Steering Committee, a 2–4 week deadline is typically given to provide ample time for review and consideration.


Annual Meeting
Each year, we will hold a meeting to review:

Steering Committee membership. We will ask if anyone is interested in stepping down from the committee and ideas for a suitable replacement.
This guidebook. We will ask the Steering Committee to review the guidebook prior to the meeting and be prepared to offer feedback on topics that should be added, edited, removed, etc.

title: Why
text:
We developed this guidebook for multiple reasons.
First, we hope that gathering important project-related information into one place will facilitate your onboarding, independence, and integration into the group. It will also act as a resource to turn to if you find yourself unsure about anything related to the team: how it functions, its origin story, etc.
Secondly, we hope that publishing this resource will increase the reproducibility of our project and decrease loss of institutional knowledge, especially since the Workflows project’s core members are contractors.

title: Why
text:
High-level, conceptual goals
Initial project planning established that a broad goal of the Workflows project was to capitalize upon recent advances in technology and improve overall assessment processes. In alignment with the 2018 Next Generation Stock Assessment Improvement Plan, our project aims to improve three of the “4Ts” of a timely, efficient, and effective stock assessment enterprise: throughput (the number of assessments that can be produced); timeliness (the speed of assessment processes and assessment product delivery), and transparency (the accessibility of assessment results). Adoption of the project’s products is also expected to improve service and trust with National Stock Assessment Program partners and stakeholders.
In parallel with these goals, we expect the workflow to decrease the amount of time and effort spent completing tasks manually, when they could be completed in a semi-automated fashion. This outcome should increase reproducibility and transparency in stock assessment workflows, in alignment of the NOAA Fisheries Open Science initiative.

title: Why
text:
Specific goals
To accomplish those high-level goals, we are focused on achieving the following objectives:

Developing a workflow based on two R packages that create stock assessment templates and media used within them
Facilitating workflow adoption by engaging in various teaching opportunities (workshops, office hours, etc.)
